item.title: QVS principal questions lack of consultation over new Deans recruitment rule
item.description: Speaking to fijivillage Sports, Nasau says any major change to one of Fiji's biggest school sporting competitions should first be discussed with school heads and trialled before being implemented. He says schools should have been given the opportunity to understand how the proposal would work, raise concerns and provide feedback before a final decision was made.
item.content:encoded:
Speaking to fijivillage Sports, Nasau says any major change to one of Fiji's biggest school sporting competitions should first be discussed with school heads and trialled before being implemented.

He says schools should have been given the opportunity to understand how the proposal would work, raise concerns and provide feedback before a final decision was made.

Nasau believes the new rule could strengthen some teams, but questions whether it will benefit school rugby in the long term.

He says allowing schools to bring in players who were not part of the team throughout the season could take away the passion, identity and sense of belonging that school rugby is built on.

Nasau says schools invest years developing players through the junior grades, making it unfair if those players lose their place to someone brought in just before the quarter-finals.

He says while new recruits may improve a team's chances on the field, they may struggle to fit into the culture, discipline and bond built by players who have trained together throughout the season.

Nasau also says the revised competition format has created additional costs and logistical challenges, with schools that qualify early now having to wait for the elimination matches to be completed instead of using that time to rest and prepare for the quarter-finals.

He says although Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby is assisting with logistics, schools are still responsible for meeting a number of other expenses.

Nasau says Queen Victoria School will respect the new rules this season but hopes Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby and school heads will review the changes once the competition concludes.

He also stresses that strict checks must be carried out to ensure any player joining a team under the new rule is a genuine student , saying the integrity of the Deans competition must be protected because the players are students first before they are rugby players.

item.content:encoded:
A journey shaped by resilience, compassion and a commitment to serving others takes centre stage on this week's fijivillage Her-Story with Temalesi Vono, as Minister for Women, Children and Social Protection Sashi Kiran shares the experiences that have defined her life.

Kiran reflects on the lessons that shaped her values, and she opens up about issues close to her heart, including violence against women and children, drugs, HIV, peacebuilding, and the importance of creating opportunities for vulnerable communities.

item.title: EMP application for beach manholes and trenching of conduits relating to proposed Natadola cable landing development declined
item.description: The Department of Environment declined the Environmental Management Plan application for the beach manholes and trenching of conduits relating to the proposed Natadola Google cable landing development in Malomalo, Nadroga on 5th February last year on the grounds of community concerns and objections, as well as insufficient social survey and public consultation information. item.content:encoded:
The Department of Environment declined the Environmental Management Plan application for the beach manholes and trenching of conduits relating to the proposed Natadola Google cable landing development in Malomalo, Nadroga on 5th February last year on the grounds of community concerns and objections, as well as insufficient social survey and public consultation information.

Ba sed on public reactions, the Ministry of Environment clarifies the proposed development forms part of the Pacific Connect initiative, a regional telecommunications programme establishing new subsea cable links between Fiji and destinations including the United States, Australia and French Polynesia.

It says the project comprises three components: the proposed Landing Station Facility, to be constructed and developed by Staghorn Services Pte Limited, the installation of two beach manholes and associated conduits leading to the landing station facility, also by Staghorn Services Pte Limited, and the Marine Subsea Cable Landing, developed and managed by Yellowfin Infrastructure Pte Limited.

Three separate EIA screening applications were lodged with the Department, one for each component.

The Environment Ministry says each was assessed on its own merits, and the components should not be reported as a single approval or a single refusal.

For the beach manholes and trenching of conduits, the Department of Environment advised the proponent that these matters must be satisfactorily addressed before further consideration can be given to the application.

The regulatory status of the other two components is that the Environmental Management Plan has been approved with conditions on 19th July 2024 for the Landing Station Facility (Staghorn Services Pte Limited) and Environmental Management Plan has been approved with conditions on 23rd September 2024 for the Marine Subsea Cable Landing (Yellowfin Infrastructure Pte Limited).

The proposed cable route is located at Natadola Bay between the Yatule Resort and Spa and the InterContinental Fiji Golf Resort and Spa and extends approximately 1.3 kilometres inland along the access road to Maro Road to the proposed Landing Station Facility site.

As part of the assessment process, a Marine Ecological Resource Assessment was undertaken in 2024 to assess potential impacts on marine habitats, fish communities, birds and water quality.

The assessment found that the marine environment within the project area is characterized by fringing coral reefs, rubble, rock and sandy substrates, with ecological communities typical of Fiji's nearshore coastal environments.

To minimize environmental impacts, the conditions imposed for the marine cable component include restricting works to daylight hours, suspending earthworks during heavy rainfall and adverse weather, protecting seagrass meadows and marine habitats, requiring prompt reporting of spills, and ensuring that cable installation activities avoid adverse impacts on coastal and marine ecosystems.

The Department also required a social survey to assess community views on the proposed development.

That requirement was imposed by the determination letter issued to Staghorn Services Pte Limited on 29th April 2024 and related specifically to the beach manholes and trenching works.

The survey, undertaken on 28th June 2024, covered residents of Sanasana Village and stall operators at Natadola Beach.

Fifty households were visited and 28 were interviewed; the remaining 22 were unwilling to respond.

Four of the households interviewed opposed the proposal, citing adverse impacts on their surroundings, on tourist activity in the area, and on their income from selling to visitors.

The other respondents did not object, provided their businesses were not affected.

The Department subsequently identified concerns regarding the adequacy of the consultation process and requested additional engagement with affected stakeholders, including Vanua Naholo, the Ministry of Lands and Mineral Resources, the iTaukei Land Trust Board and the Nadroga Provincial Office.

This consultation was facilitated through the Nadroga Provincial Office on 6th February 2025.

On that day, the Ministry of Environment made it clear that it will not involve in any compensation discussions between FNPF (that represented Google) and the vanua, as this is beyond their regulatory mandate.

During the consultations, the vanua had indicated that they would be drafting a MOA for FNPF's consideration.

The vanua also requested that the Environmental Management Plan consultant and the proponent provide an information session on the project in its entirety so that they can ask any questions, and this was relayed to the consultant.

During the consultation, further information was requested on the marine coastal assessment and the lease arrangements.

The Department relayed this request to the EMP consultant and the project proponent.

The groundbreaking ceremony went ahead in 2024 for this proposed project although the approval process was under consideration.

Permanent Secretary, Doctor Sivendra Michael had earlier said that if the Environmental Impact Assessment is under consideration for proposed projects, the private sector should not run to the ministers to get things moving and do groundbreaking ceremonies ahead of all the required approvals.

item.title: Environment Ministry says no application for hyperscale data centre by Google, no concerns on water consumption
item.description: The Ministry of Environment has today clarified that the proposed Google ICT facility has neither been applied for nor assessed as a hyperscale data centre, and the water consumption figures reported internationally for large data centres are not applicable to it. The Ministry has noted public concern about water consumption at the proposed facility, raised by reference to international reporting
item.content:encoded:
The Ministry of Environment has today clarified that the proposed Google ICT facility has neither been applied for nor assessed as a hyperscale data centre, and the water consumption figures reported internationally for large data centres are not applicable to it.

The Ministry has noted public concern about water consumption at the proposed facility, raised by reference to international reporting on data centres.

They say the development assessed by the Department of Environment is a cable landing development comprising a landing station facility, beach manholes and conduits, and a marine subsea cable landing.

The Environment Ministry says the development is similar to the facility operated by Fiji International Telecommunications Ltd (FINTEL) at Vatuwaqa, Suva , which hosts major systems such as Southern Cross NEXT and Gondwana 2.

In January 2025, Google’s Bulikula and Tabua undersea telecommunications cables were also landed at that facility.

The Ministry also says it is aware of concerns regarding activities that may be taking place within the project area.

In accordance with its regulatory responsibilities under the Environment Management Act 2005, the Ministry is prepared to undertake a compliance inspection to verify activities on the ground and determine whether all environmental approvals, approval conditions and legal requirements are being complied with.

item.title: Nadera Methodist Circuit youths commended for community clean-up initiative
item.description: The Nadera Methodist Circuit youths have been commended for their efforts in cleaning and caring for their community. The Nasinu Town Council has thanked the youths for taking the time to improve the community environment and for demonstrating what can be achieved when people come together with a shared purpose.
item.content:encoded:
The Nadera Methodist Circuit youths have been commended for their efforts in cleaning and caring for their community.

The Nasinu Town Council has thanked the youths for taking the time to improve the community environment and for demonstrating what can be achieved when people come together with a shared purpose.

The Town Council says the youths' efforts not only help create a cleaner and healthier environment but also encourage others to play their part in building stronger and safer communities.

The Council says the clean-up initiative reflects the true spirit of teamwork, unity and community pride.

It also emphasises that such activities help groom future leaders by teaching young people important values such as responsibility, service and leadership.

The youths were encouraged to continue making a positive difference in their communities, with the message noting that some of those involved today could become Fiji's future leaders.

The Nadera Methodist Circuit youths were also thanked for leading by example and demonstrating that community spirit remains strong.

item.title: LTA outlines strict new rules for provisional drivers under P1 and P2 licence system
item.description: The Land Transport Authority has outlined a series of strict rules that provisional drivers will have to follow under the new two-stage provisional licensing system, which comes into effect on 30th September 2026 . LTA says under the new system, drivers will progress through Provisional Licence 1 (P1) and Provisional Licence 2 (P2) before becoming eligible for a full driver's licence.
item.content:encoded:
The Land Transport Authority has outlined a series of strict rules that provisional drivers will have to follow under the new two-stage provisional licensing system, which comes into effect on 30th September 2026 .

LTA says under the new system, drivers will progress through Provisional Licence 1 (P1) and Provisional Licence 2 (P2) before becoming eligible for a full driver's licence.

LTA says P1 licence holders must display a red "P" sticker on both the front and rear windscreens of their vehicle.

They say drivers will only be permitted to drive between 5am and 10pm, allowed to drive private vehicles weighing less than 3.5 tonnes and are prohibited from driving hire, commercial, rental or government vehicles.

P1 drivers are also banned from towing any motor vehicle, motorcycle, motor tractor or trailer.

LTA says drivers must maintain a zero blood alcohol concentration and have no presence of illicit drugs while driving.

They further clarify that drivers progressing to Provisional Licence 2 (P2), they must display a green "P" sticker on the front and rear of their vehicle.

P2 licence holders will also be restricted to driving private vehicles weighing less than 3.5 tonnes but no any driving hour restrictions and cannot drive hire, commercial, rental or government vehicles.

T hey must continue to maintain a zero blood alcohol concentration and have no presence of illicit drugs while driving.

LTA says progression through the provisional licence stages will depend on a driver's traffic offence record.

A driver who completes the mandatory 24-month P1 period without committing any traffic offences and successfully completes the Defensive Driving Course will be eligible to apply for a full driver's licence.

However, if a P1 driver commits a traffic offence, they will be required to progress to the P2 phase and complete at least 12 months before becoming eligible for a full licence.

LTA adds that a first traffic offence will extend the provisional licence period by three months, a second offence will result in another three-month extension, while a third offence during either the P1 or P2 phase will lead to a 12-month licence suspension, after which the driver must restart the P1 process.

The Authority is also reminding vehicle owners that Traffic Infringement Notices must be transferred to the rightful driver within 90 days , as failure to do so will result in the offence being recorded against the vehicle owner, affecting a provisional licence holder's progression.

item.title: Baravi calls on youths to stay away from meth
item.description: 18 -year-old Varinisese Baravi of Macuata is urging young people to stay away from methamphetamine, saying the dangerous drug is destroying lives, families and communities. Speaking to fijivillage News during the FMF Duavata Crime Prevention Carnival, where she is representing Tanoa Electrical, Baravi says methamphetamine is a deadly drug that can take people's lives and seriously damage a person'
item.content:encoded:
18 -year-old Varinisese Baravi of Macuata is urging young people to stay away from methamphetamine, saying the dangerous drug is destroying lives, families and communities.

Speaking to fijivillage News during the FMF Duavata Crime Prevention Carnival, where she is representing Tanoa Electrical, Baravi says methamphetamine is a deadly drug that can take people's lives and seriously damage a person's health.

She says unemployment and peer pressure are among the main reasons why many young people get involved in drugs, with some spending time on the streets and eventually falling into drug abuse.

Baravi is encouraging young people to take part in sports, community activities and seek employment, saying these positive activities can help keep them away from drugs.

Her message to young people is simple: stay away from drugs and say no to methamphetamine.
